key_insight: Computable finite element bounds certify error against the original measure-valued delay law, even when computations replace that law with finitely many atoms.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports reliable simulation of diffusion with delayed principal-part response, including computations on highly anisotropic meshes.
method: Use equilibrated Raviart–Thomas fluxes to control spatial residuals.
Bound delay-law residuals through transport estimates and a cancellation-preserving cumulative-mass representation.
Include inexact equilibration and residual-mean errors, with weighted finite-horizon bounds beyond the mass-subcritical regime.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on anisotropic meshes, including a delay law beyond the mass-subcritical regime, illustrate residual-indicator behavior and efficiency limitations.
watch_item: Although reliability constants are aspect-ratio independent, the lowest-order Raviart–Thomas estimator can overestimate combined graph error by a factor growing at least proportionally to mesh aspect ratio.
paper_title: Certified Finite Element Error Bounds for Diffusion Equations with Measure-Valued Principal-Part Delays
